status: exploratory check, not the registered test
title: Cross-examine the witness: Terra's overpass time drifted
claim_text: Summer daytime land surface temperature over the Southeastern United States has risen (box 30-37N, 90W-75.5W, JJA 2001-2025)
note_on_scope: exploratory check, not the registered test. The registered result is the trend test in the case bundle; nothing on this page replaces it.

east_west_check.reading: A value near -0.067 h per degree means the field is hours UTC; near 0 would mean local solar time.

view_time.local_solar_conversion: local solar = UTC + longitude/15, applied cell by cell, then averaged with the same weights. About 85 W: box centre 82.75 W, area-weighted land centre 84.07 W, so local solar is roughly UTC minus 5.6 h.

summary.label: exploratory check, not the registered test

view_time_adjusted_lst.label: exploratory check, not the registered test

ols_with_view_time.method: OLS regression of the yearly JJA regional LST on year and the yearly JJA regional mean Day_view_time (hours): LST = a + b*year + c*view_time, n = 25, residual df = 22; 95% CI from the t distribution.

alternative_correction.method: Alternative: LST minus k*(view_time - mean 2001-2019 view_time), k = slope of (LST - POWER TS) on view time (degC per hour); then Sen slope.

summary.warning: 25 annual points and a view time that moves in one step (flat to 2019, then down); year and view time are strongly confounded, so the adjusted slope has a wide interval. It shows size and direction, not an exact correction.

method.lst: data\C-A\monthly.npz (MOD11C3 v061 LST_Day_CMG, 0.25 degree block means, land support of 1264 cells); area-weighted (cos latitude) regional mean per month, JJA mean of the three monthly means; the same series the case uses (before anomalies).
method.view_time: MOD11C3 Day_view_time (uint8, scale 0.2 h, fill 255, valid 0-120), own DAP4 request per granule, same 5x5 block mean rule (valid if >=50% of native cells valid), same support and weights; 0.9998 of support cells valid over all 75 months.
method.power: NASA POWER monthly regional, community RE, parameters TS (earth skin temperature) and T2M, tiles lon -90..-80 and -80..-75.5, lat 30-37; 279 land cells kept of 360 returned (POWER cell kept when its nearest 0.25 degree LST block is in the support); same cos-latitude weights; JJA mean of monthly regional means. MERRA-2 based, model data.
method.sen: Theil-Sen slope (scipy.stats.theilslopes, 95% interval) per decade; Mann-Kendall p from Kendall tau.
method.gap: LST minus POWER TS per year, degC (positive means MODIS warmer than the model's skin temperature).

caveats: Exploratory check, not the registered test.
POWER TS and T2M are MERRA-2 model output, not observations, and have their own inhomogeneities.
MODIS LST is clear-sky only; POWER is all-sky; a constant offset between them is expected, a changing one is what the panel looks at.

Terra's equator crossing time drifted earlier after 2020 (when orbit-maintenance burns stopped); cite NASA for that before using it in the write-up. The in-data Day_view_time series is the evidence used here.
